title: Introduce invocation observability decision tree and synthetic alert replayer
author: Ethan Brooks
description:
Motivation: We continue to see noisy alerts tied to tail invocation cost/latency signals where single noisy features (e.g. transient kernel queueing) dominate. Instead of ad-hoc suppression rules, this PR introduces a lightweight decision-tree scorer for invocation telemetry that assigns an explainable risk score and a deterministic decay policy. In addition, this PR adds a synthetic-alert replayer (replaybench) that can ingest sampled invocation logs and rerun alert scoring to validate tuning before rollouts.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds a new telemetry pipeline stage (invocation_decider) that computes invocation.decision_score and invocation.decision_reason_tags; surfaces aggregated decision histograms and cohort breakdowns to the telemetry store; ships a replaybench utility that can run historical invocation samples through the same decision logic to simulate alert churn and estimate false positive reduction; provides new Grafana dashboard panels and alert rule variants for staged rollout; adds e2e tests and unit tests, and extends CI to run the replaybench on a small synthetic dataset.

Files changed (high level): lists core scorer implementation (telemetry/decision_tree/scorer.py), replay harness (telemetry/replaybench/runner.py), sampler adapter (telemetry/adapters/sampled_ingest.py), schema migrations (telemetry/schemas/2025_11_invocation_decider.sql), dashboards (dashboards/decision-tree-invocations.json), alert rules (alerts/invocation-decision-rules.yaml), docs and runbook (docs/observability/decision-tree-runbook.md), and a small integration test (tests/integration/test_replaybench_end2end.py).

How it works: The decision-tree scorer is a shallow deterministic tree (trained offline and checked-in as a static rule set) that combines binned features: kernel_queue_ms, kv_cache_miss_ratio, prefix_length, model_variant, and cpu_percentile. The scorer produces a numeric score 0..100 and a compact set of reason tags (e.g. "queueing:high", "kv:missy"). The replaybench loads historical sampled invocations, computes scores and simulates alert triggers with current threshold configs, and reports per-cohort FP/TP estimates and expected alert volume delta.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for scorer logic and tag extraction. Integration test runs replaybench with a 20k-sample fixture (stored in test-fixtures/) and asserts alert volume reduction >= 10% without degrading recall for verified incident cases. CI change: a new workflow job (observability/replaybench) kicks off on PRs touching telemetry/ or alerts/ and runs a small synthetic dataset (fast) in CI.

Rollout plan: Canary rollout on staging telemetry ingest for 48h with decision_score exposed but not used for suppression; observability dashboard bookmarked for SRE. Next, staged alert rule variant (alpha -> beta -> global) toggled via feature flag on the console. Rollback mechanism: drop the decision flag or revert rule in the alerting engine.

Runbook and operational notes: New runbook at docs/observability/decision-tree-runbook.md documents how to interpret decision_reason_tags, query alert replays, and how to tune thresholds for specific tenants. The replaybench output includes per-tenant delta tables and recommended threshold adjustments.

Related: ENG-2382 (alert-noise-reduction), PM-4125 (observability UX for decision scores).

release_notes: Add invocation decision-tree scorer and synthetic replaybench for validating alert tuning. Exposes invocation.decision_score and invocation.decision_reason_tags; includes dashboards and staged alert variants.
migration_instructions: Run telemetry/schemas/2025_11_invocation_decider.sql against the telemetry store. Backfill is optional: run replaybench with --backfill to annotate historical invocations. Toggle decision scoring via feature flag in the console under Observability -> Feature Gates.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover scorer boundaries and tag extraction; integration test uses a 2k-sample CI fixture and a larger 20k fixture for local verification. Replaybench can be run locally: python -m telemetry.replaybench.runner --input test-fixtures/20k.ndjson --simulate-alerts --output replay-report.json
notes_for_oncall: If alert volume drops unexpectedly for a tenant after rollout, query invocation.decision_score distribution and run replaybench for that tenant ID to compare triggers. Revert alert variant via console feature flag or edit alerts/invocation-decision-rules.yaml.
benchmarks: Staging run (48h): non-actionable alert count reduced by 12% across 50 sampled tenants
Replaybench synthetic run: predicted alert volume delta -9% to -15% depending on threshold
